### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/test-typecheck-debt.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via organization_membership_ended (literal, a string literal in ApiKeyRefusalReason))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/test-typecheck-debt.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **55** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `db8124825b125adf7d50ce17bfa383253fbcd80b` — the merge of head `c534ccc5e101bbf40d84e33b1855424c4022021f` into base `9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin db8124825b125adf7d50ce17bfa383253fbcd80b && git checkout db8124825b125adf7d50ce17bfa383253fbcd80b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b c534ccc5e101bbf40d84e33b1855424c4022021f && git checkout -B drift-repro 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b && git merge --no-ff c534ccc5e101bbf40d84e33b1855424c4022021f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9b24f3ca8734b5e0ea77cc3cb282c3f8f55a862b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing at the shared key-admission seam — right.** `resolveApiKeyAdmission` (`packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts`) now returns `{ outcome: 'refused', reason: 'owner_absent', keyId, userId }` when the owner read (`ql.find('sys_user', { where: { id: userId }, fields: USER_BAN_FIELDS, limit: 1, context: { isSystem: true } })`) returns no row, and when `sys_user` is a missing table (`isMissingTableError(err, 'sys_user')` leaves `owner` undefined). The accept set loses exactly the owner-row-absent case; the admitted set is otherwise unchanged. This is the ruling, implemented where a key becomes its owner, so every door that resolves a key inherits it.
2. **Public-surface widening: `ApiKeyRefusalReason` gains `'owner_absent'` — right, and correctly declared.** The type is exported from `packages/core/src/security/index.ts` (line 176). `@objectstack/core` carries no api-surface snapshot, so no generated artifact moves. In-tree, nothing enumerates the union exhaustively: the only reader is `warnApiKeyRefusal` (`resolve-authz-context.ts`), which interpolates the reason into one log line; `membership-ended-session.ts`, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` and `storage-service-plugin.ts` name reasons in comments only. The addition is declared in prose on the `Clause-②:` line of both carriers, which is the form the closed pair allows for a mixed diff (see ②).
3. **`resolveApiKeyPrincipal` collapse — right.** It returns `undefined` for the new `refused` arm as for every other refusal (line 640). No production caller remains on it (grep over `packages/**/src` outside tests: only the re-exports in `packages/runtime/src/security/api-key.ts` and `index.ts`), so the derived behaviour is fail-closed with no live consumer to drift.
4. **`resolveAuthzContext` refused arm — unchanged and right.** The arm (lines 581–597) logs one `warnApiKeyRefusal` line and returns `anonymousEntry(ctx, input)` without reading `input.getSession`. The only edit is the comment naming the three reasons the arm now carries. So the new reason inherits: no principal, no session fall-through, the unknown-key wire answer (`401 UNAUTHENTICATED` with the same `WWW-Authenticate`), the guest entry on a guest-serving face.
5. **Every door — right.** Production call sites of the seam at this head: `resolveAuthzContext` from `packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts` (REST data door, runtime dispatcher, key-management PATCH), `packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts` (stdio: `resolveStdioExecutionContext`, and the HTTP `/mcp` door through the shared request context), `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts`, `packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts`, `packages/services/service-print/src/print-routes.ts`, `packages/cloud-connection/src/*`; and `resolveApiKeyAdmission` directly from `packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts:1348`. That last site is the ADR-0069 posture reader, not an identity door: it keeps only `held` and lets every other outcome (including the new `refused`) fall to the session's own posture gate, while identity for the same request is still decided by `resolveAuthzContext` (which refuses). This is the pre-existing shape for `owner_banned` and `organization_required`; the diff does not change it and does not need to.
6. **Ordering — right.** Lifecycle (revoked / expired / inactive) first, as ruling A requires and the pins hold; then the owner read; `owner_absent` before `owner_banned` on the same row; then `organization_required`; then the `held` posture read. An absent owner is never asked of `userAuthGates`, and `stampAdmittedKey` is never reached, so the refusal writes nothing (pinned).
7. **Store outage arm — unchanged and right.** A `sys_user` read that throws anything other than the missing-table class is still `AuthzStoreUnavailableError('sys_user')` (`503`); pinned twice in `api-key-banned-owner.test.ts`.
8. **`packages/runtime/test-typecheck-debt.json` — right.** Two entries leave the `resolve-execution-context.test.ts` row (a `TS7006` on `row` and the `TS7053` index-signature error) because the fixture's table map is now typed `Record<string, any[]>`; the ledger is shrink-only and `Type Check · debt ledger` is `success` on this head.
9. **Fixture changes (28 test files) — right, and none loosens the rule.** Every fake that serves a key row now serves its owner's `sys_user` row filtered by the id the read asks for (`where.id === OWNER` or a per-table `where` filter); none returns an owner row for an arbitrary id, and `api-key.test.ts` keeps a `users` override so an absent owner stays expressible. Two pins in `api-key-banned-owner.test.ts` flip to the new rule, named as such in the test titles.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/api-key-owner-must-exist.md`: `'@objectstack/core': patch`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Only `@objectstack/core` source moves (two files); every other changed file is a test or the runtime debt ledger, neither published. **Level matches the diff**: no authorable metadata key, value or type changes (`none` ⇒ `patch`), and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition (Post-Task Checklist step 3). `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (adr-0087 registration, no-major) are `success`.
- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right spelling.** `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines `yes (narrowing)` as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another": the public surface widens (the union member), the accept set narrows (BREAKING), and the closed pair allows one arm, so the breaking arm is the one that must be carried. The arm reader takes the first parenthetical after the value, so the trailing prose ("The widening half: …") on the same line is read as prose, not as a second arm; the gate accepted it on this head.
- The migration content a breaking changeset owes is present: who moves (an integration on an orphan key gets `401`) and the one-line remedy (mint while signed in as an existing user; revoke orphans in Setup → API Keys).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **"A store with no `sys_user` table refuses every API key."** Answered: consistent with the ruling — no owner record exists there, so no key authenticates. Judged against the tree: the missing-table class gives `refused`/`401`; a composition whose data engine throws a non-missing-table error on an unregistered `sys_user` object gives the branded `503` instead. Both refuse; neither admits; the `503` path is pre-existing and untouched by this diff. Noted, not a finding.
- **Premise check (mint path pins `user_id` to a session caller).** Verified in `packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts`: `context.admission?.credential !== 'session'` is refused (line 146) and the row is written with `user_id: ec.userId` (line 354). The orphan state is reachable only through later removal of the user row (admin remove-user, SCIM `DELETE /Users/{id}`, a direct store delete). `softDelete` was removed from the spec in 16.0 (ADR-0049), so a removed `sys_user` is a hard delete and the owner read cannot be fooled by a tombstoned row. Answered.
- **A key row with an empty `user_id` stays `none`.** Verified at `api-key.ts` line 733: `if (!userId || typeof userId !== 'string') return { outcome: 'none' }` precedes the owner read. Answered.
- **Refused key + session beside it answers `401`; made-up key + session falls through to the session.** This asymmetry is the existing refused-arm design and is what the ruling asks for (the key was presented and is refused; a session never answers for it). Pinned in core and in the dogfood door test. Answered.
- **Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write).** Expected: every GitHub write leaves through `scripts/pm/` as the fleet App. `Implemented-by:` is the branch the dispatch names, `claude/sec-hardening-r10`; the PR body's session footer is the implementing session's own attribution and is not this record's identity line.
- **Local suites NOT MEASURED at this head for `rest`, `plugin-sharing`, `service-settings`, `runtime`** (verify-lock queue timeouts, declared in the body). Not escalated: `Test Core` 8/8 shards are `success` on `c534ccc5e1` and run those suites; the record relies on the check-runs, not the body's account.
- **`Lint UI` skipped.** A paths-filter skip with no `ui/` file in the diff; whether the queue leg accepts a skipped required context is the queue guard's question, not this record's. Noted for the landing seat.
- No open question in the PR body is left unanswered.

### ④ Design judgment

Read in the live tree at `c534ccc5e101bbf40d84e33b1855424c4022021f`, judged against the ruling. Attempts to break it:

- **Every door that accepts a key.** All production doors reach `resolveApiKeyAdmission` (①.5). There is no second verifier: `sys-api-key.object.ts` names the seam as the one writer of `last_used_at` and the one reader of the hash column, and `extractApiKey` has no caller outside `api-key.ts`. Holds.
- **A session sent beside the key.** `resolveAuthzContext` returns from the refused arm before step 2 (`getSession`) is reached; `getSession` is pinned uncalled in core, and the dogfood pin sends an administrator bearer beside the orphan key on the data door and gets the made-up key's answer. Holds.
- **Ordering vs lifecycle and ban.** Lifecycle first (a revoked orphan key is refused as revoked, pinned); owner existence before the ban on the same row, so `isUserBanInForce(undefined)` is never the deciding call. Holds.
- **Store-outage arm.** Unchanged; a thrown owner read is `503`, never a refusal or an admission (pinned). Holds.
- **A store without `sys_user`.** Missing table ⇒ `owner` undefined ⇒ `refused`; pinned. Holds (see ③ for the unregistered-object `503` variant, pre-existing).
- **Fakes.** Each fixture serves the owner row only for the owner's id; no fake answers `sys_user` unconditionally. The core suite keeps a null-owner path (`makeQl(null)`, `guestServingQl({}, null)`, `users` override). Holds.
- **Nothing written on refusal.** `update` uncalled and the key row byte-equal, pinned in core; the dogfood test reads the store after every refused write. Holds.
- **Wire indistinguishability.** The dogfood pin compares status, code, message and `WWW-Authenticate` against a made-up key on data read, data write, key-management PATCH and MCP initialize. Holds.
- **Operator line.** One `[security] API key refused (owner_absent)` line naming `key=` row id and `principal=` owner id, from the single decision point in `resolve-authz-context.ts`; never the raw key or hash. Pinned to exactly one line per refused request. Holds.
- **ADR citation.** The code cites ADR-0090's note that an API key is its owner's credential, not an agent principal (ADR-0090 lines 440, 583). The citation holds.

**Findings**

- should-fix (non-blocking, comment drift): the `ApiKeyRefusalReason` docblock in `packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts` (lines 492–495) still says a refusal "means the credential is real and intact but cannot be admitted under this deployment's tenancy posture". With `owner_banned` and now `owner_absent` on the union, two of four reasons are owner-standing refusals, not posture refusals. One sentence to correct; the `ApiKeyAdmission` docblock below it already reads right.
- must-fix: none.
